#tab-switch: Stage 0: the switch. One switch turns a lamp on and off, and everything else is built from it.
#tab-gates: Stage 1: logic gates. Wire switches together to make AND, OR, NOT and XOR, then package each one as a module.
#tab-half: Stage 2: the half adder. Add two single bits with just an XOR gate and an AND gate, using the gate modules from Stage 1.
#tab-full: Stage 3: the full adder. Two half adders and an OR gate add two bits plus a carry coming in. It reuses the half adder module from Stage 2.
#tab-ripple: Stage 4: the 8-bit adder. Eight full adders in a row, each passing its carry to the next. Each one is the full adder module from Stage 3.
#a0: Bit 0 of A, worth 1. Click to flip it between 0 and 1. This is the least significant bit, on the far right.
#a1: Bit 1 of A, worth 2. Click to flip it between 0 and 1.
#a2: Bit 2 of A, worth 4. Click to flip it between 0 and 1.
#a3: Bit 3 of A, worth 8. Click to flip it between 0 and 1.
#a4: Bit 4 of A, worth 16. Click to flip it between 0 and 1.
#a5: Bit 5 of A, worth 32. Click to flip it between 0 and 1.
#a6: Bit 6 of A, worth 64. Click to flip it between 0 and 1.
#a7: Bit 7 of A, worth 128. Click to flip it between 0 and 1. This is the most significant bit, on the far left. In signed numbers it is the sign bit.
#b0: Bit 0 of B, worth 1. Click to flip it between 0 and 1. This is the least significant bit, on the far right.
#b1: Bit 1 of B, worth 2. Click to flip it between 0 and 1.
#b2: Bit 2 of B, worth 4. Click to flip it between 0 and 1.
#b3: Bit 3 of B, worth 8. Click to flip it between 0 and 1.
#b4: Bit 4 of B, worth 16. Click to flip it between 0 and 1.
#b5: Bit 5 of B, worth 32. Click to flip it between 0 and 1.
#b6: Bit 6 of B, worth 64. Click to flip it between 0 and 1.
#b7: Bit 7 of B, worth 128. Click to flip it between 0 and 1. This is the most significant bit, on the far left. In signed numbers it is the sign bit.
#cin: Carry-in: an extra 1 added to the total when it is on. Turn it on to add A + B + 1.
#aDec: A as an ordinary number. Type any whole number from 0 to 255 and the bits above update to match.
#bDec: B as an ordinary number. Type any whole number from 0 to 255 and the bits above update to match.
#aHex: A in hexadecimal (base 16), two digits from 00 to FF. Type here to set A; each digit stands for four bits.
#bHex: B in hexadecimal (base 16), two digits from 00 to FF. Type here to set B; each digit stands for four bits.
#sum: The 8-bit result of A + B + carry-in, shown in binary, decimal and hex. Anything past 255 shows up as the carry-out instead.
#cout: Carry-out: lights up when the true total is more than 255 and does not fit in 8 bits. The sum then shows the total minus 256.
#overflow: Signed overflow: lights up when the bits are read as signed numbers (-128 to 127) and the answer falls outside that range.
#mode: How the circuit settles: Instant shows the answer at once, Slow plays it out one step at a time, and Step waits for you to press Next step.
#step: Move forward one step: the signals pass through one more layer of gates. Works in Step mode.
#speed: How fast Slow mode plays. Slide left to slow it down, right to speed it up.
#random: Pick new random values for A and B.
#reset: Set A, B and carry-in back to 0 and start over.
#zoom: Choose one bit position (0 to 7) to see its full adder up close, with its truth table and the current row lit up.
#sw: Click to flip the switch. Closed lets current through and lights the lamp (1); open turns it off (0).
#gateA: Input A for the gate. Click to flip it between 0 and 1.
#gateB: Input B for the gate. Click to flip it between 0 and 1. NOT uses only one input, so B is hidden or ignored when NOT is picked.
#gatePick: Choose which gate to build: AND, OR, NOT or XOR.
#symbolToggle: Switch between seeing the gate as wired-up switches and as its standard symbol. Both views work exactly the same.
#package: Fold the circuit back up into modules: blocks that show only their inputs and outputs. Use Expand to look inside again.
#expand: Open the module one layer to see what it's made of. On the Gates stage you can go all the way down to switches; on the adder stages it stops at gate symbols.
#haA: Input A for the half adder. Click to flip it between 0 and 1.
#haB: Input B for the half adder. Click to flip it between 0 and 1.
#faA: Input A for the full adder. Click to flip it between 0 and 1.
#faB: Input B for the full adder. Click to flip it between 0 and 1.
#faC: Carry-in for the full adder: the carry that would come from the column to its right. Click to flip it between 0 and 1.
